deduped_items.title: Женщина угнала у угонщиков свою угнанную машину
deduped_items.body_text:
В Великобритании мать троих детей нашла и угнала свою машину у воров, воспользовавшись приложением на iPhone, чтобы отследить оставленный в багажнике ноутбук. Об этом сообщает Daily Mail.
38-летняя Виви Кала и ее муж Дэвид оставили свой автомобиль Kia Sportage на улице возле отеля Prince Regent в Чигвелле, графство Эссекс, вечером 20 августа, пока сами были на свадьбе. Когда через четыре часа они вышли из отеля, машины на месте не было. В багажнике остались детские игрушки и MacBook Pro. Муж начал звонить в полицию, а Виви запустила приложение для поиска связанных устройств на смартфоне и увидела, что ноутбук находится на другом краю города.
Женщина вызвала такси, объяснила водителю ситуацию, после чего они отправились на поиски ноутбука. По пути она показала таксисту карту с геолокацией, и тот быстро доставил их к цели. Муж вышел из машины первым, а Виви осталась в такси на случай, если угонщики еще рядом. Сначала они не были уверены, что нашли свою машину, — воры успели поменять номерные знаки, установив поддельные с номерами и адресом автосалона Kia.
К счастью, автомобиль не был поврежден, и семья просто открыла его и уехала. Они смогли отправиться в запланированный отпуск в Шотландию уже на следующий день. Кала призналась, что если бы не ноутбук в багажнике, найти машину было бы практически невозможно. Теперь она собирается купить противоугонный замок на руль и специальный трекер.
Ранее сообщалось, что в США арестовали мужчину, который угнал машину скорой помощи. Он сел за руль припаркованной машины, будучи полностью голым. В этот момент два медика находились в салоне и оказывали помощь пациенту.

deduped_items.title: Пезешкиан рассказал, когда Иран вернется к выполнению меморандума с США
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Президент Ирана Масуд Пезешкиан заявил, что Тегеран вернется к выполнению меморандума о прекращении огня с Вашингтоном, как только США сделают это.
БИШКЕК, 1 сен - РИА Новости. Тегеран вернется к выполнению меморандума о прекращении огня с Вашингтоном, как только США сделают это, заявил президент Ирана Масуд Пезешкиан. 
США и Израиль 28 февраля начали наносить удары по объектам на территории Ирана, на что иранская сторона ответила своими ударами. В середине июня Тегеран и Вашингтон подписали меморандум о прекращении боевых действий, однако через некоторое время вновь обменялись ударами. В настоящий момент конфликт остается неурегулированным.

deduped_items.title: В Москве колесо оторвалось от машины и попало в пешехода
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- В результате ДТП на востоке Москвы колесо оторвалось от машины.
- Колесо попало в пешехода.
МОСКВА, 1 сен - РИА Новости. Колесо оторвалось от машины в результате ДТП и попало в пешехода на востоке Москвы, сообщили РИА Новости в правоохранительных органах. 
"В результате ДТП колесо оторвалось от машины", - сказал собеседник агентства. 
По его словам, оно попало в пешехода.

deduped_items.title: Больше, чем торговля. Как Россия и Индия перестраивают партнерство
deduped_items.summary: Российско-индийское партнерство постепенно выходит за привычные рамки торговли нефтью, чаем и лекарствами. На смену приходит новая модель: совместные производства, инвестиции и технологии. Где лежат эти возможности – обсудили на сессии Сбера на ВЭФ.
deduped_items.body_text:
Российско-индийский бизнес, похоже, решил не складывать «все яйца» в одну корзину. Торговля между странами растет, но теперь речь все чаще идет не только о сырье, лекарствах и традиционных товарах. На первый план выходят машиностроение, электроника, химия, IT, биотехнологии, совместные фармацевтические разработки, инвестиции и даже недвижимость.
Есть и вполне конкретные результаты. Например, товарооборот Дальнего Востока с Индией в первом полугодии вырос на 50%. Еще российский бизнес осваивает индийский рынок, а индийские компании все активнее смотрят в сторону наших регионов. Именно об этом — как превратить хорошие политические отношения в устойчивые деловые связи и совместные технологические проекты — говорили на бизнес-ланче Сбера «Экспертный диалог „Россия-Индия: развитие технологического партнерства для повышения устойчивости бизнеса“». Модерировал сессию первый заместитель председателя правления ПАО Сбер Александр Ведяхин.
Индия открывает двери
Один из главных выводов встречи — инвесторам пора смотреть на Индию шире. Речь уже не только о том, куда продать российский товар или что привезти из Индии. Растущий индийский рынок сам становится объектом вложений.
Индийская сторона рассчитывает упростить доступ российских инвесторов к своему фондовому рынку. Среди инструментов — работа через международный финансовый центр GIFT City, где действуют специальные условия для бизнеса и инвесторов. Звучала и идея расширять линейку финансовых продуктов, чтобы индийские активы становились понятнее и доступнее российским клиентам.
Интересно, что для Сбера это не теория. Банк уже инвестирует в индийскую экономику и развивает там собственную инфраструктуру.
Отдельная история — недвижимость. Рынок коммерческой недвижимости Индии растет стремительно, особенно в крупнейших городах. Сбер, в частности, приобрел две крупные башни в центре Дели, напротив Всемирного торгового центра. Завершить их строительство планируется в 2028 году. Там разместится штаб-квартира Сбера в Индии, а сам объект рассматривается как будущая точка притяжения для российского бизнеса. Получается своеобразный мост: российская компания приходит в Индию не с чемоданом визиток, а с собственной площадкой, финансовыми инструментами и готовой инфраструктурой.
Дальний Восток — окно в Индию

deduped_items.summary: Российско-индийское партнерство постепенно выходит за привычные рамки торговли нефтью, чаем и лекарствами. На смену приходит новая модель: совместные производства, инвестиции и технологии. Где лежат эти возможности – обсудили на сессии Сбера на ВЭФ.
deduped_items.body_text:
Российско-индийский бизнес, похоже, решил не складывать «все яйца» в одну корзину. Торговля между странами растет, но теперь речь все чаще идет не только о сырье, лекарствах и традиционных товарах. На первый план выходят машиностроение, электроника, химия, IT, биотехнологии, совместные фармацевтические разработки, инвестиции и даже недвижимость.
Есть и вполне конкретные результаты. Например, товарооборот Дальнего Востока с Индией в первом полугодии вырос на 50%. Еще российский бизнес осваивает индийский рынок, а индийские компании все активнее смотрят в сторону наших регионов. Именно об этом — как превратить хорошие политические отношения в устойчивые деловые связи и совместные технологические проекты — говорили на бизнес-ланче Сбера «Экспертный диалог „Россия-Индия: развитие технологического партнерства для повышения устойчивости бизнеса“». Модерировал сессию первый заместитель председателя правления ПАО Сбер Александр Ведяхин.
Индия открывает двери
Один из главных выводов встречи — инвесторам пора смотреть на Индию шире. Речь уже не только о том, куда продать российский товар или что привезти из Индии. Растущий индийский рынок сам становится объектом вложений.
Индийская сторона рассчитывает упростить доступ российских инвесторов к своему фондовому рынку. Среди инструментов — работа через международный финансовый центр GIFT City, где действуют специальные условия для бизнеса и инвесторов. Звучала и идея расширять линейку финансовых продуктов, чтобы индийские активы становились понятнее и доступнее российским клиентам.
Интересно, что для Сбера это не теория. Банк уже инвестирует в индийскую экономику и развивает там собственную инфраструктуру.
Отдельная история — недвижимость. Рынок коммерческой недвижимости Индии растет стремительно, особенно в крупнейших городах. Сбер, в частности, приобрел две крупные башни в центре Дели, напротив Всемирного торгового центра. Завершить их строительство планируется в 2028 году. Там разместится штаб-квартира Сбера в Индии, а сам объект рассматривается как будущая точка притяжения для российского бизнеса. Получается своеобразный мост: российская компания приходит в Индию не с чемоданом визиток, а с собственной площадкой, финансовыми инструментами и готовой инфраструктурой.
Дальний Восток — окно в Индию
Своя ставка есть и у российских регионов. Причем Дальний Восток здесь явно не собирается оставаться статистом. По словам первого заместителя министра по развитию Дальнего Востока и Арктики Виталия Алабаева, в первом полугодии товарооборот Дальнего Востока с Индией вырос на 50%. В прошлом году он составлял около 700 млн долларов, и по итогам 2026 года ожидается дальнейший рост.
Особые надежды возлагаются на международные территории опережающего развития и инновационный технологический центр на острове Русский. Первый корпус уже построен, еще два — для IT, биотехнологических и других технологических проектов — находятся в работе. И здесь интересы двух стран сходятся почти без натяжки: Индия сильна в IT, биотехнологиях и фармацевтике, а Россия предлагает площадки, ресурсы и доступ к собственным рынкам.
«Мы готовим нормативную базу, создаем новые площадки и хотим, чтобы индийские инвесторы приходили сюда. Особенно интересны нам IT, биотехнологии и фармацевтика — именно те направления, в которых индийский бизнес традиционно силен», — отметил Виталий Алабаев.
Торговля меняет ассортимент
Еще несколько лет назад разговор об индийском импорте в Россию был довольно предсказуемым: чай, рис, фрукты, текстиль и лекарства. Сегодня список заметно расширяется. Руководитель Сбера в Индии Иван Носов назвал главным словом последних лет «диверсификация». По его словам, за последние годы линейка индийских товаров, которые российские компании рассматривают для закупок, выросла примерно в 3-4 раза. При этом общий объем поставок увеличился примерно на 20%.
И вот тут начинается самое интересное. Речь идет уже не просто о большем количестве товаров, а о появлении совершенно новых категорий.

Российско-индийский бизнес, похоже, решил не складывать «все яйца» в одну корзину. Торговля между странами растет, но теперь речь все чаще идет не только о сырье, лекарствах и традиционных товарах. На первый план выходят машиностроение, электроника, химия, IT, биотехнологии, совместные фармацевтические разработки, инвестиции и даже недвижимость.
Есть и вполне конкретные результаты. Например, товарооборот Дальнего Востока с Индией в первом полугодии вырос на 50%. Еще российский бизнес осваивает индийский рынок, а индийские компании все активнее смотрят в сторону наших регионов. Именно об этом — как превратить хорошие политические отношения в устойчивые деловые связи и совместные технологические проекты — говорили на бизнес-ланче Сбера «Экспертный диалог „Россия-Индия: развитие технологического партнерства для повышения устойчивости бизнеса“». Модерировал сессию первый заместитель председателя правления ПАО Сбер Александр Ведяхин.
Индия открывает двери
Один из главных выводов встречи — инвесторам пора смотреть на Индию шире. Речь уже не только о том, куда продать российский товар или что привезти из Индии. Растущий индийский рынок сам становится объектом вложений.
Индийская сторона рассчитывает упростить доступ российских инвесторов к своему фондовому рынку. Среди инструментов — работа через международный финансовый центр GIFT City, где действуют специальные условия для бизнеса и инвесторов. Звучала и идея расширять линейку финансовых продуктов, чтобы индийские активы становились понятнее и доступнее российским клиентам.
Интересно, что для Сбера это не теория. Банк уже инвестирует в индийскую экономику и развивает там собственную инфраструктуру.
Отдельная история — недвижимость. Рынок коммерческой недвижимости Индии растет стремительно, особенно в крупнейших городах. Сбер, в частности, приобрел две крупные башни в центре Дели, напротив Всемирного торгового центра. Завершить их строительство планируется в 2028 году. Там разместится штаб-квартира Сбера в Индии, а сам объект рассматривается как будущая точка притяжения для российского бизнеса. Получается своеобразный мост: российская компания приходит в Индию не с чемоданом визиток, а с собственной площадкой, финансовыми инструментами и готовой инфраструктурой.

Своя ставка есть и у российских регионов. Причем Дальний Восток здесь явно не собирается оставаться статистом. По словам первого заместителя министра по развитию Дальнего Востока и Арктики Виталия Алабаева, в первом полугодии товарооборот Дальнего Востока с Индией вырос на 50%. В прошлом году он составлял около 700 млн долларов, и по итогам 2026 года ожидается дальнейший рост.
Особые надежды возлагаются на международные территории опережающего развития и инновационный технологический центр на острове Русский. Первый корпус уже построен, еще два — для IT, биотехнологических и других технологических проектов — находятся в работе. И здесь интересы двух стран сходятся почти без натяжки: Индия сильна в IT, биотехнологиях и фармацевтике, а Россия предлагает площадки, ресурсы и доступ к собственным рынкам.
«Мы готовим нормативную базу, создаем новые площадки и хотим, чтобы индийские инвесторы приходили сюда. Особенно интересны нам IT, биотехнологии и фармацевтика — именно те направления, в которых индийский бизнес традиционно силен», — отметил Виталий Алабаев.
Торговля меняет ассортимент
Еще несколько лет назад разговор об индийском импорте в Россию был довольно предсказуемым: чай, рис, фрукты, текстиль и лекарства. Сегодня список заметно расширяется. Руководитель Сбера в Индии Иван Носов назвал главным словом последних лет «диверсификация». По его словам, за последние годы линейка индийских товаров, которые российские компании рассматривают для закупок, выросла примерно в 3-4 раза. При этом общий объем поставок увеличился примерно на 20%.

Germany's SPD is fighting for survival
September 1, 2026
The Social Democratic Party SPD is sinking ever deeper into crisis. Voters are turning away, while unrest is growing within its grassroots ranks. Will the upcoming state elections accelerate the party's downward spiral?
At a fitness class run by the Workers' Welfare Association, one stop on his tour through Saxony-Anhalt, Matthias Miersch is giving it his all: Hands up, hands down, touch your toes, all in time to the German schlager hit "Regenbogenfarben."
Miersch, leader of the center-left Social Democratic Party's (SPD) parliamentary group, has travelled to Saxony-Anhalt for a 24-hour visit to lend his support.
The election campaign in the eastern German state has entered its decisive final phase. In the state capital of Magdeburg and three smaller towns, he meets with SPD state politicians and local residents, taking part in discussions with a queer advocacy organization, a housing cooperative, and an initiative dedicated to the social integration of young refugees.
Everything revolves around the party's core issues: affordable housing, social support, poverty reduction, integration, and protection against discrimination based on sexual identity. At the Rainbow Café in Magdeburg, Miersch speaks openly about his own sexual identity as a gay man. Those gathered there describe the open hatred and hostility they encounter, especially in rural areas, and speak of their growing fear of the prospect of a state government led by the Alternative for Germany (AfD).
The AfD's Saxony-Anhalt branch has been classified by the domestic intelligence agency as a confirmed right-wing extremist organisation. "We are witnessing a rollback of the freedoms and lifestyles that have emerged over recent decades," Miersch says at the Rainbow Café. The small room is colourful and crowded; on a shelf sit small flags bearing the slogan "No Time for Nazis."
The SPD cannot stop the AfD
The Social Democrats have little with which to counter the AfD's rise in Saxony-Anhalt. Germany's oldest political party is polling at just 7-8%, compared to the AfD's 42%. The SPD's main concern is that it might even fall below the 5% threshold for representation in parliament. The reason for the dwindling support is that many voters feel the party no longer has a clearly defined identity.
The SPD is the junior coalition partner in the deeply unpopular federal government alongside the center-right Christian Democratic Union and Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU).
"I do not want to conceal the fact," Miersch tells the journalists travelling with him at the end of the tour, "that federal politics is also fuelling debate here on the ground." What he is referring to above all is the planned reform of the statuary pension system, especially the proposal to abolish the option of early retirement after 45 years, often referred to as retirement at 63. For many residents of Saxony-Anhalt, which has long grappled with an ageing population and demographic decline, the proposal is a particularly contentious issue.
Elections in five federal states
Yet Saxony-Anhalt is not the only place where the SPD is battling decline. Nationwide, the party is polling at only around 12%, trailing the AfD, the CDU/CSU, and the Greens. The situation is even more acute in some individual states. With elections in five of Germany's sixteen states and city-states, 2026 is a super election year. Two of those contests have already taken place.
The results so far are sobering: in the south-western state of Baden-Württemberg, the SPD recorded its worst result of the postwar era and only just managed to retain its representation in the state parliament. deduped_items.title: Liveticker zur Landtagswahl Merz hält an der Brandmauer fest, Handwerksverband warnt vor der AfD
deduped_items.summary: Wenige Tage vor den Landtagswahlen in Sachsen-Anhalt ist die Stimmung aufgeheizt. Erstmals könnte die AfD eine Regierung übernehmen. Merz betont die Stabilität der Brandmauer, während sein Parteifreund Kretschmer mit einer Minderheitsregierung rechnet. Lesen Sie hier alle Entwicklungen im Liveticker. Dieser Beitrag Liveticker zur Landtagswahl Merz hält an der Brandmauer fest, Handwerksverband warnt vor der AfD wurde veröffentlich auf JUNGE FREIHEIT.
deduped_items.body_text:
14.30 Uhr: Der evangelische Landesbischof für Mitteldeutschland, Friedrich Kramer, hat vor einer AfD-Regierung in Sachsen-Anhalt gewarnt. In einem solchen Fall würden „Rechtsextreme plötzlich auf der Straße noch brutaler auf andere Menschen zugehen würden, die anders aussehen“, prognostizierte Kramer im Gespräch mit dem Sender Phoenix.
„Die Folgen werden vor allem für alles, was Menschen mit Migrationshintergrund anbelangt, die ganzen Remigrationsphantasien der AfD – und der Spitzenkandidat steht ja für das Potsdamer treffen – verheerend.“ Viele Bürger würden freiwillig das Land verlassen, „ohne, dass sie rausgeschickt werden“, zeigte sich Kramer überzeugt.
Das hätte für die Sozialversorgung, die Pflege und das Gastronomiegewerbe „Riesenfolgen, die sofort zu spüren sind“, sagte der Landesbischof. Auch das „Frauenbild“ der AfD und die Haltung zur „queeren Community“ kritisiert Kramer scharf. Hier gebe es „ganze Kulturbereiche, die in der Programmatik der AfD massiv beschnitten und auf Linie gebracht werden“ sollten.
Ebenso aus der katholischen Kirche kommt lautstarke Kritik an der AfD. So ist der Bischof von Magdeburg, Gerhard Feige, Mitinitiator der Kampagne „Bewusst Wählen“ und betet laut eigener Aussage dafür, dass die AfD es in Sachsen-Anhalt nicht in die Regierung schafft.
14 Uhr: In Sachsen-Anhalt herrscht große Nachfrage nach der Briefwahl. Bis zum 25. August wurden etwa 335.000 Briefwahlunterlagen versendet, wie das Statistische Landesamt am Dienstag mitteilte. Das sind etwa 20 Prozent aller Wahlberechtigten in Sachsen-Anhalt.
Bei den vergangenen Landtagswahlen im Jahr 2021 hatten lediglich 315.567 Personen ihre Stimme per Briefwahl abgegeben.
Zuletzt hatten doppelt versendete Wahlunterlagen in Halle und der Landeshauptstadt Magdeburg für Kritik gesorgt (JF berichtete).
13.30 Uhr: Die linksextreme Gruppe „Widersetzen“ hat mit Blick auf die Landtagswahlen in Sachsen-Anhalt zu mehreren Veranstaltungen aufgerufen. So soll am kommenden Donnerstag in Halle eine Demonstration namens „Halle steht auf“ stattfinden, am Samstag soll es zwei weitere Veranstaltungen geben: In Magdeburg geht es nach Angaben der Organisatoren darum, „Haltung zu zeigen für Demokratie, Vielfalt und Zusammenhalt“. Am selben Tag ist in Halle eine „Antifaschistische Vorabdemo zur Landtagswahl“ angemeldet.
Am Wahlabend selbst sollen ab 18.30 Uhr mehrere „dezentrale Demos“ stattfinden, wie die Verantwortlichen von „Widersetzen“ auf ihrem Instagram-Kanal mitteilen.
Die Gruppe „Widersetzen“ wurde im April 2024 gegründet und sorgte Ende Juni desselben Jahres für weitreichende Empörung, weil es bei der Gründungsveranstaltung der AfD-Jugendorganisation Generation Deutschland zu massiven Ausschreitungen vonseiten der „Widersetzen“-Teilnehmer gekommen war. Im Juni dieses Jahres griffen linksextreme Demonstranten aus dem „Widersetzen“-Umfeld beim AfD-Bundesparteitag in Erfurt Reporter von „Apollo News“ und der JUNGEN FREIHEIT körperlich an.
Darauf angesprochen distanzierten sich die Verantwortlichen nicht von politischer Gewalt, im Gegenteil. „Widersetzen“-Sprecher Noa Sander sagte dazu: „Faschisten mit einem Presseausweis sind immer noch Faschisten.“
13 Uhr: Bundeskanzler Merz hat mit Blick auf mögliche Mehrheitsverhältnisse in Sachsen-Anhalt die Brandmauer zu AfD und Linkspartei bekräftigt. „Sowohl bei AfD als auch bei der Linkspartei gibt es derart fundamentale Unterschiede zur Union, dass eine Zusammenarbeit ausgeschlossen ist“, sagte er der Mitteldeutschen Zeitung und der Magdeburger Volksstimme.
Auf die Frage, ob eine Minderheitsregierung unter CDU-Führung im Landtag auf wechselnde Mehrheiten bauen sollte, sagte der Bundeskanzler: „Wir sehen, wie in Thüringen und Sachsen regiert werden kann. Aber es muss auch klar sein, dass es Grenzen gibt.“ Es werde keine Zusammenarbeit mit AfD und Linkspartei geben, unterstrich Merz.
In Thüringen und Sachsen greifen die CDU-Ministerpräsidenten Mario Voigt und Michael Kretschmer regelmäßig auf Stimmen der Linkspartei zurück

„Die Folgen werden vor allem für alles, was Menschen mit Migrationshintergrund anbelangt, die ganzen Remigrationsphantasien der AfD – und der Spitzenkandidat steht ja für das Potsdamer treffen – verheerend.“ Viele Bürger würden freiwillig das Land verlassen, „ohne, dass sie rausgeschickt werden“, zeigte sich Kramer überzeugt.
Das hätte für die Sozialversorgung, die Pflege und das Gastronomiegewerbe „Riesenfolgen, die sofort zu spüren sind“, sagte der Landesbischof. Auch das „Frauenbild“ der AfD und die Haltung zur „queeren Community“ kritisiert Kramer scharf. Auf die Frage, ob eine Minderheitsregierung unter CDU-Führung im Landtag auf wechselnde Mehrheiten bauen sollte, sagte der Bundeskanzler: „Wir sehen, wie in Thüringen und Sachsen regiert werden kann. Aber es muss auch klar sein, dass es Grenzen gibt.“ Es werde keine Zusammenarbeit mit AfD und Linkspartei geben, unterstrich Merz.

„Die Folgen werden vor allem für alles, was Menschen mit Migrationshintergrund anbelangt, die ganzen Remigrationsphantasien der AfD – und der Spitzenkandidat steht ja für das Potsdamer treffen – verheerend.“ Viele Bürger würden freiwillig das Land verlassen, „ohne, dass sie rausgeschickt werden“, zeigte sich Kramer überzeugt.
Das hätte für die Sozialversorgung, die Pflege und das Gastronomiegewerbe „Riesenfolgen, die sofort zu spüren sind“, sagte der Landesbischof. Aber es muss auch klar sein, dass es Grenzen gibt.“ Es werde keine Zusammenarbeit mit AfD und Linkspartei geben, unterstrich Merz.
In Thüringen und Sachsen greifen die CDU-Ministerpräsidenten Mario Voigt und Michael Kretschmer regelmäßig auf Stimmen der Linkspartei zurück

deduped_items.title: Jane Fonda and Gisèle Pelicot among winners of 2026 DVF Awards in Venice
deduped_items.summary: Barbados Prime Minister, journalist Addario, Wawira Njiru of Food4Education also honoured
deduped_items.body_text:
Jane Fonda and Gisèlle Pelicot are
among the recipients of the 17th Diane von Furstenberg awards at
this year's Venice Film Festival.
                                    
                                       
				Actress and activist Fonda; Barbados Prime Minister Mia Amor
Mottley; photojournalist Lynsey Addario; Food4Education Founder
and CEO Wawira Njiru; and multiple rape survivor, author and
activist Pelicot are the winners of the "DVF Awards," promoted
by 79-year-old fashion designer von Furstenberg to recognize
women global leaders, activists, artists, and changemakers of
extraordinary talent.
                                    
                                       
				The awards ceremony will be held in Venice on
September 3.
                                    
                                       
				Over the years, the DVF Awards have given voice and visibility
to women from more than thirty countries,
supporting their work through financial contributions to promote
initiatives in a variety of fields, from the fight against
climate change and human trafficking, to the promotion of gender
equality and the prevention of
violence against women.
                                    
                                       
				The five winners of the 2026 DVF Awards, a statement emphasizes,
"represent extraordinary examples of
people capable of transforming their beliefs into action and
generating concrete change.
                                    
                                       
				From environmental protection to political leadership, from
frontline journalism to commitment to nutrition and education,
to the defense of the dignity and rights of victims of violence,
the work of the five winners testifies to the extraordinary
strength and variety of impact women can have when they turn
determination into action."
"For the 17th year of the DVF Awards, I'm thrilled to honor
women who have the courage to fight, the strength to survive,
and the leadership to inspire," says von Furstenberg.

deduped_items.body_text:
Jane Fonda and Gisèlle Pelicot are
among the recipients of the 17th Diane von Furstenberg awards at
this year's Venice Film Festival.
                                    
                                       
				Actress and activist Fonda; Barbados Prime Minister Mia Amor
Mottley; photojournalist Lynsey Addario; Food4Education Founder
and CEO Wawira Njiru; and multiple rape survivor, author and
activist Pelicot are the winners of the "DVF Awards," promoted
by 79-year-old fashion designer von Furstenberg to recognize
women global leaders, activists, artists, and changemakers of
extraordinary talent.
                                    
                                       
				The awards ceremony will be held in Venice on
September 3.
                                    
                                       
				Over the years, the DVF Awards have given voice and visibility
to women from more than thirty countries,
supporting their work through financial contributions to promote
initiatives in a variety of fields, from the fight against
climate change and human trafficking, to the promotion of gender
equality and the prevention of
violence against women.
                                    
                                       
				The five winners of the 2026 DVF Awards, a statement emphasizes,
"represent extraordinary examples of
people capable of transforming their beliefs into action and
generating concrete change.
                                    
                                       
				From environmental protection to political leadership, from
frontline journalism to commitment to nutrition and education,
to the defense of the dignity and rights of victims of violence,
the work of the five winners testifies to the extraordinary
strength and variety of impact women can have when they turn
determination into action."
"For the 17th year of the DVF Awards, I'm thrilled to honor
women who have the courage to fight, the strength to survive,
and the leadership to inspire," says von Furstenberg.

deduped_items.title: Jane Fonda and Gisèle Pelicot among winners of 2026 DVF Awards in Venice
deduped_items.summary: Barbados Prime Minister, journalist Addario, Wawira Njiru of Food4Education also honoured
deduped_items.body_text:
Jane Fonda and Gisèlle Pelicot are
among the recipients of the 17th Diane von Furstenberg awards at
this year's Venice Film Festival.
                                    
                                       
				Actress and activist Fonda; Barbados Prime Minister Mia Amor
Mottley; photojournalist Lynsey Addario; Food4Education Founder
and CEO Wawira Njiru; and multiple rape survivor, author and
activist Pelicot are the winners of the "DVF Awards," promoted
by 79-year-old fashion designer von Furstenberg to recognize
women global leaders, activists, artists, and changemakers of
extraordinary talent.
                                    
                                       
				The awards ceremony will be held in Venice on
September 3.
                                    
                                       
				Over the years, the DVF Awards have given voice and visibility
to women from more than thirty countries,
supporting their work through financial contributions to promote
initiatives in a variety of fields, from the fight against
climate change and human trafficking, to the promotion of gender
equality and the prevention of
violence against women.
                                    
                                       
				The five winners of the 2026 DVF Awards, a statement emphasizes,
"represent extraordinary examples of
people capable of transforming their beliefs into action and
generating concrete change.
                                    
                                       
				From environmental protection to political leadership, from
frontline journalism to commitment to nutrition and education,
to the defense of the dignity and rights of victims of violence,
the work of the five winners testifies to the extraordinary
strength and variety of impact women can have when they turn
determination into action."
"For the 17th year of the DVF Awards, I'm thrilled to honor
women who have the courage to fight, the strength to survive,
and the leadership to inspire," says von Furstenberg.

deduped_items.body_text:
Salomé Pradas cambia de abogado para afrontar la fase decisiva de la instrucción de la dana
La exconsellera de Emergencias ficha al penalista Pedro Colina tras la desvinculación del letrado Eduardo de Urbano por motivos personales
Valencia
La exconsellera de Justicia e Interior de la Generalitat Valenciana Salomé Pradas ha reestructurado su equipo de defensa ante la fase decisiva de la investigación judicial sobre la gestión de la dana del 29 de octubre de 2024 con el fichaje del prestigioso ... penalista Pedro Colina, ahora en el despacho Kepler-Karts. El relevo se produce en un momento especialmente relevante de la instrucción que dirige la juez de Catarroja Nuria Ruiz Tobarra, que mantiene a la extitular de Emergencias como investigada.
Según ha confirmado fuentes de la defensa de Pradas a ABC, la exconsellera afronta la continuación de la instrucción bajo la nueva defensa de Colina, junto a las penalistas Sandra Imedio y Paloma Crespo. Por su parte, el exmagistrado y abogado Eduardo Urbano se desliga del equipo judicial por motivos personales, sin descartar volver a intervenir de nuevo en el futuro.
Kepler-Karst define a Colina, procedente del bufete Choclán, como uno de los principales especialistas de España en materia de Derecho Penal Económico, con más de tres décadas de experiencias en algunos de los procedimientos penales de mayor complejidad y repercusión mediática. Hasta ahora, encabezaba la representación del exsecretario de Estado de Seguridad Francisco Martínez en la causa de la 'Operación Kitchen'.
Colina es licenciado en Derecho por la Universidad Complutense de Madrid y Máster en Gestión de Empresa por la CEOE. Es profesor asociado de Derecho Penal en la Universidad Carlos III de Madrid e imparte docencia en diversos Másteres de Acceso al Ejercicio de la Abogacía (ICADE, Universidad Cisneros y Universidad Carlos III). Es coautor del Código Penal Comentado y con Jurisprudencia (La Ley), principal obra de referencia doctrinal en Derecho Penal de España, y ponente habitual en la Escuela de Práctica Jurídica de la Universidad Complutense.
El nuevo mandato de Colina no supone una ruptura completa de la defensa de Pradas, pues seguirán con él las penalistas Imedio y Crespo. El movimiento llega en un momento donde la causa judicial afronta una de las etapas de mayor trascendencia. La magistrada de Catarroja mantiene abiertas diligencias contra Pradas y su número dos en Emergencias, Emilio Argüeso.
Los abogados de la exconsellera se han mostrado especialmente críticos con la instrucción de la juez Rui Tobarra, llegando a cuestionar su imparcialidad objetiva. Trasladó un escrito al Consejo General del Poder Judicial (CGPJ) para criticar que la juez estaba prolongando «artificialmente» la investigación llamando a declarar como testigo a «todo aquel que haya tenido el más mínimo contacto con los hechos», al tiempo que ignora cualquier otra vía que contradiga su «tesis preestablecida»: la «desidia o inactividad de los investigados y el retraso en enviar los ES-Alert».
Pradas apuntó a la instructora por, a su juicio, la «visión sesgada» y «bajo prejuicios» con la que está investigando lo ocurrido. «Mientras se practican diligencias que arrojan luz sobre la inocencia o la atenuación de responsabilidad de mi mandante, la instructora mantiene sus criterios iniciales sin el menor rubor, como si las diligencias de prueba que se van practicando, no existieran», cuestionó.
Para su defensa, la juez ha adoptado una «tesis de culpabilidad prematura» con «juicios de valor lapidarios, la filtración sistemática de actuaciones que genera un juicio paralelo lesivo para la reputación de la investigada, y una actitud hostil hacia los informes de la Policía Judicial que contradicen su visión de los hechos, lo que en conjunto supone un ejercicio desequilibrado de la función jurisdiccional en una causa de gran trascendencia social».

deduped_items.body_text:
El delegado del Gobierno en Castilla y León: «Lo importante en la A-11 no es la lista de invitados»
«Se ha estado esperando más de tres décadas, pero ha sido el trabajo de ministro Óscar Puente quien ha impulsado sin ninguna duda la actuación», ha declarado Sen
Mónica S. Blanco
Valladolid
«Lo que realmente tiene valor es la puesta en funcionamiento de un tramo más de esta autovía y no una lista de invitados», ha expresado el delegado del Gobierno en Castilla y León, el socialista Nicanor Sen, sobre la denuncia por parte del PP ... de que en el acto de inauguración de la A-11 en Valladolid estuviera presuntamente invitado el secretario autonómico del PSOE, Carlos Martínez, y no el presidente de la Junta de Castilla y León, Alfonso Fernández Mañueco, o los alcaldes de los pueblos de la zona. En cuanto a si la Junta de Castilla y León fue invitada al acto, Sen se ha remitido a las palabras del ministro de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible, Óscar Puente a los medios de comunicación, recalcando el delegado que «lo importante aquí es poner en valor el tramo que se ha abierto».
En relación con la posibilidad de que la posible laxitud a la hora de terminar la autovía del Duero, por la que hay quejas de los vecinos desde hace 30 años y accidentes anuales, Sen ha explicado que «precisamente porque los vecinos llevan más de tres décadas esperando por esta autovía», se debe hablar de «la importancia de la puesta en funcionamiento de esos 30,7 kilómetros en sentido Valladolid y de esos 25,5 kilómetros en sentido Soria».
Asimismo, después de hacer balance de las actuaciones del Ejecutivo central en la Comunidad hasta el primer semestre de 2026, el delegado ha señalado que la autovía «es diariamente utilizada por cientos y cientos de usuarios que atraviesan nuestro territorio», lo que contibuye a que sea «una de las vías de alta capacidad más importantes que tenemos en Castilla y León». «Creo que aquí eh las explicaciones las dio perfectamente el ministro de Transportes», ha dicho en referencia a «poner de relieve el valor de esta importante obra», pues «lo que realmente tiene valor son los kilómetros abiertos, la inversión realizada y la mejora en la seguridad para todos y cada uno de los usuarios».
Noticia relacionada
«Se ha estado esperando más de tres décadas, pero ha sido el gobierno de Pedro Sánchez y, en concreto, el trabajo de ministro Óscar Puente, quien ha impulsado sin ninguna duda la actuación de esta importante vía de alta velocidad en nuestra comunidad autónoma», ha descrito el delegado. Además, ha descrito que «todos hemos podido ver el otro día en la inauguración de este nuevo tramo que las obras del otro tramo consecutivo avanzan a buen ritmo», por lo que «esperemos que a lo largo del año 2027 se le pueda dar una continuidad a la mejora».
Balance
El delegado ha presentado el informe Cumpliendo, el instrumento de rendición de cuentas del Gobierno de España que recoge el grado de ejecución de los principales compromisos del Ejecutivo en la Comunidad durante el primer semestre de 2026.
Durante su intervención, Sen ha puesto en valor el alcance de las inversiones y medidas impulsadas por el Gobierno de España en Castilla y León, destacando que la Comunidad ha recibido ya más de 5.260 millones de euros procedentes del Plan de Recuperación, Transformación y Resiliencia, resultado de la suma de los 1.873 millones de euros asignados a la Junta de Castilla y León y los 3.388 millones ejecutados directamente por la Administración General del Estado desde su puesta en marcha en julio de 2020. «De estos fondos, se han podido beneficiar 88.615 empresas, instituciones y ciudadanas y ciudadanos», ha subrayado.

deduped_items.body_text:
EXPOSICIÓN
San Esteban reúne en el Ayuntamiento de Sevilla los bustos vinculados con el Señor de la Salud y Buen Viaje
El alcalde de Sevilla, José Luis Sanz, ha anunciado que una de las portadas del Corpus de 2027 estará dedicada a esta hermandad
La hermandad de San Esteban ha inaugurado, con el inicio del mes de septiembre, en el Ayuntamiento de Sevilla, la exposición «La devoción que construye una historia. San Esteban 1926-2026», enmarcada dentro de los actos conmemorativos de su centenario fundacional, que ... la corporación celebra durante este año. Es la segunda muestra celebrada tras la llevada a cabo a primeros de año en el Círculo Mercantil e Industrial de Sevilla.
Se trata de «una exposición singular», como así ha declarado el comisario de la muestra, Javier Rodríguez Barberán. La idea surgió de la curiosidad de indagar sobre el centro de la devoción de esta hermandad como es el Señor de la Salud y Buen Viaje y querer acerarse sin prejuicios a sus orígenes.
Para el comisario de la exposición, Javier Rodríguez Barberán, como señaló durante la presentación, «resulta interesante asomarnos a un mundo menos conocido y, en ocasiones, menos valorado: el de la adaptación de piezas anónimas. El Señor es una pieza anónima que atesora un atractivo viaje a través del tiempo. Originalmente era un busto de terracota que, hace un siglo, se convirtió en la devoción principal de la hermandad».
La muestra, instalada en el patio mayor del Ayuntamiento de Sevilla, reúne varios bustos procedentes de distintos puntos de España que presentan semejanzas con el Señor de la Salud y Buen Viaje de San Esteban. Posiblemente, estas imágenes anónimas, incluido el titular de San Esteban, tengan un origen común, tanto en el tiempo como en el espacio.
Los bustos ubicados en la exposición provienen del antiguo convento de Santo Domingo de Toledo, del museo de Antequera, Sevilla, Sanlúcar de Barrameda y la Campana, siendo este último restaurado recientemente para la muestra de San Esteban. Asimismo, este incorpora un recorrido por la creación artística de imágenes devocionales del siglo XVI y por la evolución de esta iconografía.
Estas obras «van a permitir verla desde todos los puntos de vista y darle un contexto, explicando en los paneles algo que es normalmente poco conocido y necesario de subrayar: la producción de las imágenes devocionales y el destino del tiempo», ha apuntado Javier Rodríguez Barberán.
En un principio, como indicó el comisario de la muestra, estaba previsto que estuvieran presentes otros bustos procedentes de Lima, Ayacucho y de una colección particular de Italia, aunque finalmente no ha sido posible contar con ellos.
El alcalde de Sevilla, José Luis Sanz, durante su intervención, ha destacado en la presentación de la exposición el significado que tiene para la ciudad la celebración del centenario de esta hermandad y su vinculación con uno de los grandes referentes de la Semana Santa sevillana. «Es para mí un verdadero honor inaugurar en el Ayuntamiento de Sevilla, vuestra casa, esta exposición, una muestra que nos invita a mirar con otros ojos una devoción profundamente arraigada en Sevilla y que, desde hace cien años, forma parte de la memoria sentimental, religiosa y cofrade de nuestra ciudad», ha señalado Sanz.
En este sentido, Sanz ha puesto en valor que la exposición permita descubrir «una parte quizá menos conocida de ese patrimonio devocional: los bustos del Señor de la Salud y Buen Viaje que se conservan en distintos puntos de Sevilla y de Andalucía», unas piezas que, a su juicio, «hablan de la capacidad de una imagen, de una iconografía, para trascender los límites de una iglesia y de una hermandad y convertirse en parte de la identidad colectiva».
Portada del Corpus
Por otro lado, el alcalde de Sevilla, ha dado a conocer que una de las portadas del Corpus Christi de 2027 estará dedicada a la hermandad de San Esteban por su centenario.
La portada tendrá como inspiración y modelo la imponente portada mudéjar de la iglesi

deduped_items.body_text:
Salomé Pradas cambia de abogado para afrontar la fase decisiva de la instrucción de la dana
La exconsellera de Emergencias ficha al penalista Pedro Colina tras la desvinculación del letrado Eduardo de Urbano por motivos personales
Valencia
La exconsellera de Justicia e Interior de la Generalitat Valenciana Salomé Pradas ha reestructurado su equipo de defensa ante la fase decisiva de la investigación judicial sobre la gestión de la dana del 29 de octubre de 2024 con el fichaje del prestigioso ... penalista Pedro Colina, ahora en el despacho Kepler-Karts. El relevo se produce en un momento especialmente relevante de la instrucción que dirige la juez de Catarroja Nuria Ruiz Tobarra, que mantiene a la extitular de Emergencias como investigada.
Según ha confirmado fuentes de la defensa de Pradas a ABC, la exconsellera afronta la continuación de la instrucción bajo la nueva defensa de Colina, junto a las penalistas Sandra Imedio y Paloma Crespo. Por su parte, el exmagistrado y abogado Eduardo Urbano se desliga del equipo judicial por motivos personales, sin descartar volver a intervenir de nuevo en el futuro.
Kepler-Karst define a Colina, procedente del bufete Choclán, como uno de los principales especialistas de España en materia de Derecho Penal Económico, con más de tres décadas de experiencias en algunos de los procedimientos penales de mayor complejidad y repercusión mediática. Hasta ahora, encabezaba la representación del exsecretario de Estado de Seguridad Francisco Martínez en la causa de la 'Operación Kitchen'.
Colina es licenciado en Derecho por la Universidad Complutense de Madrid y Máster en Gestión de Empresa por la CEOE. Es profesor asociado de Derecho Penal en la Universidad Carlos III de Madrid e imparte docencia en diversos Másteres de Acceso al Ejercicio de la Abogacía (ICADE, Universidad Cisneros y Universidad Carlos III). Es coautor del Código Penal Comentado y con Jurisprudencia (La Ley), principal obra de referencia doctrinal en Derecho Penal de España, y ponente habitual en la Escuela de Práctica Jurídica de la Universidad Complutense.
El nuevo mandato de Colina no supone una ruptura completa de la defensa de Pradas, pues seguirán con él las penalistas Imedio y Crespo. El movimiento llega en un momento donde la causa judicial afronta una de las etapas de mayor trascendencia. La magistrada de Catarroja mantiene abiertas diligencias contra Pradas y su número dos en Emergencias, Emilio Argüeso.
Los abogados de la exconsellera se han mostrado especialmente críticos con la instrucción de la juez Rui Tobarra, llegando a cuestionar su imparcialidad objetiva. Trasladó un escrito al Consejo General del Poder Judicial (CGPJ) para criticar que la juez estaba prolongando «artificialmente» la investigación llamando a declarar como testigo a «todo aquel que haya tenido el más mínimo contacto con los hechos», al tiempo que ignora cualquier otra vía que contradiga su «tesis preestablecida»: la «desidia o inactividad de los investigados y el retraso en enviar los ES-Alert».
Pradas apuntó a la instructora por, a su juicio, la «visión sesgada» y «bajo prejuicios» con la que está investigando lo ocurrido. «Mientras se practican diligencias que arrojan luz sobre la inocencia o la atenuación de responsabilidad de mi mandante, la instructora mantiene sus criterios iniciales sin el menor rubor, como si las diligencias de prueba que se van practicando, no existieran», cuestionó.
Para su defensa, la juez ha adoptado una «tesis de culpabilidad prematura» con «juicios de valor lapidarios, la filtración sistemática de actuaciones que genera un juicio paralelo lesivo para la reputación de la investigada, y una actitud hostil hacia los informes de la Policía Judicial que contradicen su visión de los hechos, lo que en conjunto supone un ejercicio desequilibrado de la función jurisdiccional en una causa de gran trascendencia social».

deduped_items.title: The three witnesses to Lorenzo Salgado’s death are free as the case moves toward a grand jury
deduped_items.summary: The district attorney in the Texas county where the Mexican migrant was killed says he hopes to reinterview the passengers who witnessed the shooting, including Salgado’s brother Víctor, now that they are out of detention and can speak freely without fear of being monitored
deduped_items.body_text:
The three witnesses to Lorenzo Salgado’s death are free as the case moves toward a grand jury
The district attorney in the Texas county where the Mexican migrant was killed says he hopes to reinterview the passengers who witnessed the shooting, including Salgado’s brother Víctor, now that they are out of detention and can speak freely without fear of being monitored
Shortly after 10:15 a.m. on Sunday, Víctor Salgado was able to embrace his family for the first time after 54 days in detention at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility in Houston. During those 54 days, he repeatedly relived the operation in which his brother, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, was fatally shot by an ICE agent. His attorney, Ruby L. Powers, visited him minutes after he returned home. She found a man who was “relieved and grateful,” but who was also beginning to grieve — a process that had been put on hold during his detention.
Powers did not disclose the conditions of Salgado’s release, including whether he had been fitted with an ankle monitor, as the other two material witnesses were. She said, however, that he is focused on recovering from weeks of detention so that he can participate, from outside custody, in the investigation being led by the Harris County District Attorney’s Office.
“He wants to be available for that process. He knows the district attorney needs him for the grand jury,” Powers told EL PAÍS. She added that her last conversation with Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare took place last week.
In Texas, a grand jury, which is made up of ordinary citizens, determines whether there is enough evidence to bring formal charges against a person.
Víctor Salgado, 44, was one of three migrants traveling with Lorenzo Salgado to a construction job on July 7 when ICE agents began pursuing them. The operation ended with Lorenzo Salgado being shot and taken to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The three witnesses, meanwhile, were handcuffed and taken to the same detention facility, though they were kept separated from one another.
In recent weeks, two of those witnesses, José Trinidad Rojas, 51, and Daniel Tirado Pantoja, 43, were released following habeas corpus petitions filed by their attorneys. With Víctor Salgado’s release from ICE custody, the county’s investigation into the operation enters a new phase, one that has raised expectations within both the local community and Salgado Araujo’s family.
The road to a grand jury
In an interview on Houston Public Media on Friday, District Attorney Sean Teare outlined the next steps in the investigation into Lorenzo Salgado’s death.
Investigators have already interviewed the three witnesses while they were being held at the Montgomery ICE Processing Center. But Teare said that he wants to speak with them again, now that they are free “in a clean place […] where they’re not worried someone might be listening.”
The district attorney’s office plans to present their testimony “soon,” along with the rest of the evidence, to a grand jury in the near future. The panel will then decide what charges, if any, should be brought, and against whom, in connection with the death of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo.
“We are at an inflection point. In material terms, when you talk about the evidence generated that day, we’ve reached the point where we have obtained practically everything we could,” he said.
Through its digital forensics unit and investigators who spent an entire month on the ground, Taere said, the office collected surveillance footage from cameras in the community and interviewed witnesses, allowing it to reconstruct ICE’s pursuit of Salgado’s van and the events that unfolded after the shooting.

During those 54 days, he repeatedly relived the operation in which his brother, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, was fatally shot by an ICE agent. His attorney, Ruby L. Powers, visited him minutes after he returned home. She found a man who was “relieved and grateful,” but who was also beginning to grieve — a process that had been put on hold during his detention.
Powers did not disclose the conditions of Salgado’s release, including whether he had been fitted with an ankle monitor, as the other two material witnesses were. She said, however, that he is focused on recovering from weeks of detention so that he can participate, from outside custody, in the investigation being led by the Harris County District Attorney’s Office.
“He wants to be available for that process. He knows the district attorney needs him for the grand jury,” Powers told EL PAÍS. She added that her last conversation with Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare took place last week.
In Texas, a grand jury, which is made up of ordinary citizens, determines whether there is enough evidence to bring formal charges against a person.

During those 54 days, he repeatedly relived the operation in which his brother, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, was fatally shot by an ICE agent. His attorney, Ruby L. Powers, visited him minutes after he returned home. She found a man who was “relieved and grateful,” but who was also beginning to grieve — a process that had been put on hold during his detention.
Powers did not disclose the conditions of Salgado’s release, including whether he had been fitted with an ankle monitor, as the other two material witnesses were. She said, however, that he is focused on recovering from weeks of detention so that he can participate, from outside custody, in the investigation being led by the Harris County District Attorney’s Office.
“He wants to be available for that process. He knows the district attorney needs him for the grand jury,” Powers told EL PAÍS. She added that her last conversation with Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare took place last week.
In Texas, a grand jury, which is made up of ordinary citizens, determines whether there is enough evidence to bring formal charges against a person.

During those 54 days, he repeatedly relived the operation in which his brother, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, was fatally shot by an ICE agent. His attorney, Ruby L. Powers, visited him minutes after he returned home. She found a man who was “relieved and grateful,” but who was also beginning to grieve — a process that had been put on hold during his detention.
Powers did not disclose the conditions of Salgado’s release, including whether he had been fitted with an ankle monitor, as the other two material witnesses were. She said, however, that he is focused on recovering from weeks of detention so that he can participate, from outside custody, in the investigation being led by the Harris County District Attorney’s Office.
“He wants to be available for that process. He knows the district attorney needs him for the grand jury,” Powers told EL PAÍS. She added that her last conversation with Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare took place last week.
In Texas, a grand jury, which is made up of ordinary citizens, determines whether there is enough evidence to bring formal charges against a person.

During those 54 days, he repeatedly relived the operation in which his brother, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, was fatally shot by an ICE agent. His attorney, Ruby L. Powers, visited him minutes after he returned home. She found a man who was “relieved and grateful,” but who was also beginning to grieve — a process that had been put on hold during his detention.
Powers did not disclose the conditions of Salgado’s release, including whether he had been fitted with an ankle monitor, as the other two material witnesses were. She said, however, that he is focused on recovering from weeks of detention so that he can participate, from outside custody, in the investigation being led by the Harris County District Attorney’s Office.
“He wants to be available for that process. He knows the district attorney needs him for the grand jury,” Powers told EL PAÍS. She added that her last conversation with Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare took place last week.
In Texas, a grand jury, which is made up of ordinary citizens, determines whether there is enough evidence to bring formal charges against a person.

During those 54 days, he repeatedly relived the operation in which his brother, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, was fatally shot by an ICE agent. His attorney, Ruby L. Powers, visited him minutes after he returned home. She found a man who was “relieved and grateful,” but who was also beginning to grieve — a process that had been put on hold during his detention.
Powers did not disclose the conditions of Salgado’s release, including whether he had been fitted with an ankle monitor, as the other two material witnesses were. She said, however, that he is focused on recovering from weeks of detention so that he can participate, from outside custody, in the investigation being led by the Harris County District Attorney’s Office.
“He wants to be available for that process. He knows the district attorney needs him for the grand jury,” Powers told EL PAÍS. She added that her last conversation with Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare took place last week.
In Texas, a grand jury, which is made up of ordinary citizens, determines whether there is enough evidence to bring formal charges against a person.

During those 54 days, he repeatedly relived the operation in which his brother, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, was fatally shot by an ICE agent. His attorney, Ruby L. Powers, visited him minutes after he returned home. She found a man who was “relieved and grateful,” but who was also beginning to grieve — a process that had been put on hold during his detention.
Powers did not disclose the conditions of Salgado’s release, including whether he had been fitted with an ankle monitor, as the other two material witnesses were. She said, however, that he is focused on recovering from weeks of detention so that he can participate, from outside custody, in the investigation being led by the Harris County District Attorney’s Office.
“He wants to be available for that process. He knows the district attorney needs him for the grand jury,” Powers told EL PAÍS. She added that her last conversation with Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare took place last week.
In Texas, a grand jury, which is made up of ordinary citizens, determines whether there is enough evidence to bring formal charges against a person.

The operation ended with Lorenzo Salgado being shot and taken to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The three witnesses, meanwhile, were handcuffed and taken to the same detention facility, though they were kept separated from one another.

deduped_items.title: Dutch Cabinet minister wants churches to help fill the thousands of healthcare vacancies
deduped_items.summary: Long-term Care Minister Mirjam Sterk wants churches to do more to relieve the burden on the healthcare system, she said during the Willibrord Lecture at the opening of the academic year o
deduped_items.body_text:
Dutch Cabinet minister wants churches to help fill the thousands of healthcare vacancies
Long-term Care Minister Mirjam Sterk wants churches to do more to relieve the burden on the healthcare system, she said during the Willibrord Lecture at the opening of the academic year of the Protestant Theological University in Utrecht on Monday. Churches can help fill the thousands of vacancies in the healthcare sector if they stop focusing on caring for the soul alone, she said, Trouw reports.
In recent decades, more and more of the care burden has fallen on the government, while churches turned to lobbying and criticising, Sterk said. She called on churches to focus less on “care for the soul” and commit themselves to the “caring society” - a society in which people help and support each other more so that they rely less on the overburdened healthcare sector.
The Dutch healthcare sector is facing massive shortages. In the coming decade, the number of open vacancies in the sector is expected to increase to over 300,000 care providers - more people than the residents of Eindhoven. “Now that you see the government can no longer provide all the care, I think churches need to think about how they can fill that gap, as they did in the past,” Sterk told Trouw.
“The churches have often degenerated into commenters on the government’s shortcomings in the areas of care, welfare, and asylum. Without truly stepping in themselves and thinking through how old concepts such as community, mercy, and justice can be developed into new concepts like self-reliance or compassion,” the Minister told Trouw.
“I don’t know if they did that consciously, but churches have really fallen back on caring for the soul. In my work as Healthcare Minister, I encounter spiritual caregivers in prisons and care institutions. But otherwise, I don’t see the church anywhere anymore.”
She added that she’s not asking churches to start providing medical care. “Healthcare reforms are also very much about how to shape caring communities together. Churches can certainly contribute to this by being more outward-looking than inward-looking. For example, by organizing activities that are very accessible. It is more about supporting people; think, for instance, of having coffee with people with mental health issues.”

Long-term Care Minister Mirjam Sterk wants churches to do more to relieve the burden on the healthcare system, she said during the Willibrord Lecture at the opening of the academic year of the Protestant Theological University in Utrecht on Monday. Churches can help fill the thousands of vacancies in the healthcare sector if they stop focusing on caring for the soul alone, she said, Trouw reports.
In recent decades, more and more of the care burden has fallen on the government, while churches turned to lobbying and criticising, Sterk said. She called on churches to focus less on “care for the soul” and commit themselves to the “caring society” - a society in which people help and support each other more so that they rely less on the overburdened healthcare sector.
The Dutch healthcare sector is facing massive shortages. In the coming decade, the number of open vacancies in the sector is expected to increase to over 300,000 care providers - more people than the residents of Eindhoven. “Now that you see the government can no longer provide all the care, I think churches need to think about how they can fill that gap, as they did in the past,” Sterk told Trouw.
“The churches have often degenerated into commenters on the government’s shortcomings in the areas of care, welfare, and asylum. Without truly stepping in themselves and thinking through how old concepts such as community, mercy, and justice can be developed into new concepts like self-reliance or compassion,” the Minister told Trouw.
“I don’t know if they did that consciously, but churches have really fallen back on caring for the soul. In my work as Healthcare Minister, I encounter spiritual caregivers in prisons and care institutions. But otherwise, I don’t see the church anywhere anymore.”
She added that she’s not asking churches to start providing medical care. “Healthcare reforms are also very much about how to shape caring communities together. Churches can certainly contribute to this by being more outward-looking than inward-looking. For example, by organizing activities that are very accessible. It is more about supporting people; think, for instance, of having coffee with people with mental health issues.”

deduped_items.title: Groningen University launches Frisian language degree
deduped_items.summary: Groningen University has launched a bachelor’s degree programme in the Frisian language, the first standalone course in the country’s second...
deduped_items.body_text:
Groningen University launches Frisian language degree
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
Groningen University has launched a bachelor’s degree programme in the Frisian language, the first standalone course in the country’s second official language for 15 years.
Three students began the course this week, which covers linguistics, history and Frisian culture. Frisian was taught as a degree in its own right until 2012, when it was absorbed into a broader programme on Europe’s minority languages, Minorities & Multilingualism.
That programme drew too few students to survive and the university said it would phase it out from the 2025/26 academic year, leaving the academic study of Frisian at risk of vanishing altogether.
A rescue from The Hague
 The course was saved after the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW) recommended, in a report on the future of Frisian studies, that the state pay for a dedicated bachelor. The government agreed to put in €340,000 a year, with further provincial money.
For legal reasons the new degree sits as a Frisian track within the university’s Dutch Languages and Cultures programme, though the focus is now entirely on Frisian.
Professor of Frisian Arjen Versloot said he was happy with the intake, even though a course usually needs around 20 students to break even. “There are often only five students in French and German too, so as a small language we can’t complain,” he told regional broadcaster Omrop Fryslân.
Teachers in demand
 The degree is also meant to supply qualified teachers. Since August, schools in Friesland have been required to use more Frisian in the classroom under new curriculum rules, and Versloot expects strong demand for teachers able to deliver it at the highest level.
Frisian is spoken by around 470,000 people in Friesland and is the closest living relative of English.
Reading and writing proficiency in Frisian has risen sharply over the past two decades, despite fewer people speaking the language at home, according to a recent survey.
Around 58% of residents in Friesland now say they can read Frisian well or very well, up from 46% in 2007. Self-reported writing proficiency nearly doubled over the same period, from 9.6% to 18.9%.

deduped_items.title: National Museum Unveils Rare 16th-Century Silver Coins Found at Somló Hill
deduped_items.summary: A special exhibition titled “Thaler Hoard Discovered at the Foot of Somló Hill” opened Monday at the Hungarian National Museum. During an archaeological excavation carried out in Veszprém County in the summer of 2026 in cooperation with the institution’s volunteer archaeological team, researchers discovered 27 early modern silver thalers. The unusual archaeological finds will be […] The post National Museum Unveils Rare 16th-Century Silver Coins Found at Somló Hill appeared first on Hungary Toda
deduped_items.body_text:
The collection is particularly notable for its gold ornaments, a rarity among Conquest-era finds.Continue reading
A special exhibition titled “Thaler Hoard Discovered at the Foot of Somló Hill” opened Monday at the Hungarian National Museum. During an archaeological excavation carried out in Veszprém County in the summer of 2026 in cooperation with the institution’s volunteer archaeological team, researchers discovered 27 early modern silver thalers. The unusual archaeological finds will be on display at the museum through October 18, it was announced at the opening of the exhibition.
Gábor Zsigmond, director general of the Hungarian National Museum, said the institution considers the development of volunteer work a priority and established its Community Archaeology Department to organize and coordinate such activities through its volunteer program.
He also noted that the National Museum is hosting a three-day international numismatic conference from Monday through Wednesday.
Held for the 11th time, the conference provides leading researchers in the field with an opportunity to present their latest research in numismatics.
Historian Teréz Oborni, an associate professor at the Faculty of Humanities at Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), emphasized that the exhibition is particularly interesting as Hungary has just commemorated the 500th anniversary of the Battle of Mohács. The thalers date from the period that followed the battle, including the era of the Long Turkish War.
The museum said in a statement that it has been conducting successful research in the Somló area of Veszprém County for several years.
The vast majority of the coins—18 in total—were minted by Archduke Ferdinand II of Austria, at the mint in Hall in Tirol and in Ensisheim in Alsace.
The hoard also contained three thalers issued by Holy Roman Emperor Rudolf II: two Hungarian and one Bohemian. The German territories were represented by two coins minted by the city of Lübeck, as well as one thaler each from the Palatinate, Brunswick and Brandenburg. The hoard was further complemented by a thaler from the Swiss city of St. Gallen.
The youngest coin in the hoard, known in numismatic terminology as the closing coin, is a thaler minted by Rudolf II in Kremnica in 1593. The value of the hoard and the relative proportions of the different issues suggest that it can be linked to the Long Turkish War (1591/1593–1606). The series of military campaigns that took place year after year over roughly a decade and a half extended across the entire Carpathian Basin. Hoards from this period provide direct evidence of the scale of the destruction and preserve a record of the diverse currency circulation of the era.
Via MTI, Featured image: MTI/Kovács Márton

deduped_items.title: Hiába formalitás, minden korábbinál nagyobb kihívás a Kremlnek a háború alatti első parlamenti választás
deduped_items.summary: Az Ukrajna ellen indított háború nem Putyin tervei szerint halad, amit egyre nehezebb elfedni az állami propagandával. Sokatmondó az orosz vezetés növekvő arroganciája saját polgárai felé, és egyre többször merül fel, lesz-e mozgósítás a választás után. Ezt az orosz vezetés a tagadás ellenére nem tudja meggyőzően kizárni.

September 19: Celebrate South Africa's Heritage Braai Day in Prague
Prague Morning
On Saturday, 19 September, Prague’s Rohan Beer Garden will host Heritage Braai Day, bringing the flavors and traditions of South Africa to the city.
The event is organized by Saffa Maso.
From noon, visitors can enjoy a relaxed day of grilling, music and socializing outdoors.
Heritage Day in South Africa is a public holiday celebrating the country’s cultural diversity. It has also become closely associated with the tradition of braai, or South African-style barbecuing, with friends and family gathering around the grill to share food.
In Prague, the event is open to everyone and will feature multiple grills, allowing visitors to prepare their own food. Those who prefer to leave the cooking to someone else can use the on-site grill master service, available for an additional fee.
Standard tickets include grills, coals and all braai equipment. Visitors can also choose a braai package, which includes 500g of traditional boerewors sausage and 150g of biltong.
On-site, guests will also be able to purchase Nando’s sauces, chutney, braai spices and other South African products.
Visitors should not bring their own drinks, as a selection of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages will be available at the venue. Guests should bring their own plates and cutlery, although disposable options are also allowed.
Tickets are available via SMSTicket at this link. Children under 12 enter free.

deduped_items.body_text:
Prague Philharmonic Could Begin Construction in 2028. New Visuals Reveal Design
Prague Morning
Prague has taken another step toward building the long-planned Vltava Philharmonic.
The Prague Development Company (PDS) submitting an application for planning permission and new visualizations revealing the project in greater detail.
The application covers not only the Philharmonic building but also the surrounding public spaces, transport infrastructure and connections to the existing metro, tram, road, cycling and pedestrian networks.
If the permitting process stays on schedule, the city expects to receive the necessary approval in the first quarter of 2027. A tender for the construction company would then follow, with building work potentially starting in the first quarter of 2028.
The project is planned for the Bubny-Zátory district, near the existing Vltavská metro station. The new cultural complex is expected to be completed in 2033, when trial operations could begin.
The building was designed by Danish architecture studio BIG – Bjarke Ingels Group, which won an international competition in May 2022. Preparation of the detailed permit documentation began in 2025.
The complex will have three underground levels and six floors above ground. It will contain five music halls, creative spaces, restaurants and other facilities.
The project is also intended to provide new premises for the Prague Symphony Orchestra FOK and music collections belonging to the Municipal Library of Prague. The Czech Philharmonic is also expected to gain additional facilities, addressing the limitations of its current premises.
Construction could start in early 2028
The current estimated cost of the Philharmonic building is around CZK 12.33 billion, including equipment but excluding VAT. The surrounding infrastructure and public spaces are expected to cost an additional CZK 5 billion, also excluding VAT.

Tiny Steps, Big Milestones: What Really Matters When Toddlers Start Preschool
Prague Morning
For a one-year-old, starting preschool is not about learning letters or sitting through lessons.
It is about feeling safe without Mum or Dad nearby, discovering the joy of playing alongside other children, and slowly gaining the confidence to explore the world independently. At Tiny Tots in Prague, these small everyday moments are at the heart of the programme.
A favourite toy clutched tightly in one hand. A cautious look back at Mum or Dad from the classroom door. Perhaps a few tears (from either side).
For families with children aged one or two, the first experience of leaving a little one in someone else’s care can feel like a very big step.
And for the child, it is one too.
At this age, development happens through moments that can look almost insignificant to adults: reaching for a spoon without help, joining another child in play, recognising a familiar song, saying a new word, or feeling comfortable enough to wander a little further away from a trusted adult.
These are precisely the moments that Tiny Tots, a programme for children aged 1–2 at Nessie English Preschool, part of Park Lane International School, is designed to encourage.
Before learning comes feeling safe
For very young children, a good first preschool experience begins with something much more fundamental than an academic curriculum: trust.
“Parents often want to know how their child will cope with separation, whether we can follow the rhythm they are used to at home and, above all, whether their child will really be seen as an individual,” says Catalina Gonzalez-Got, who leads the Tiny Tots programme.
Catalina knows the feeling from both sides. An early-years educator with international experience, she is also a mother herself. Becoming a parent, she says, gave her a much deeper understanding of how emotional it can be to entrust a young child to somebody else for the first time.
That is why settling in is treated as a process rather than a test that a toddler is expected to pass on day one.
Some children may quickly become curious about their new surroundings. Others need more time, reassurance and proximity to a familiar adult before they are ready to explore.
Both are perfectly normal. The goal is to allow each child to find that confidence at their own pace.
For toddlers, play is serious business
Adults sometimes separate “playing” and “learning”. Toddlers do not.
When a child squishes playdough between their fingers, listens to a story, sings along to a familiar song, explores the garden or watches another toddler build something, they are constantly learning.
They are practising movement and coordination. They are discovering cause and effect. They are learning how to communicate, negotiate space with other children, manage emotions and make choices.
Tiny Tots therefore follows a play-based approach inspired by the English Early Years Foundation Stage framework, with activities designed around the developmental needs of one- and two-year-olds.
There are no miniature school desks or pressure to perform.
Instead, children encounter language, movement, music, creative activities, sensory experiences, stories and outdoor play as a natural part of their day.
The programme keeps the class to a maximum of eight children, allowing teachers to pay close attention to individual personalities, routines and developmental stages.
English without the flashcards
The same philosophy applies to language.
At one or two years old, learning English does not mean memorising vocabulary lists. Children absorb language through relationships and repetition: hearing the same words during snack time, listening to songs, following simple instructions, sharing a picture book or hearing an adult describe what is happening during play.
Tiny Tots provides an English-language environment, giving children regular, natural exposure to the language throughout their day.

deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            Ministry maximizing defense spendingMILITARY BUILDUP: Aside from this year’s budget, the defense ministry detailed its mid-term plan to upgrade, develop and procure defense materiel amid Chinese threats
  - By William Hetherington / Staff writer, with CNA
 The military is reviewing budget execution trends and postponing non-urgent projects to maximize defense spending, the Ministry of National Defense said yesterday as it submitted its budget for next year and other defense documents to the legislature. The ministry said China’s “gray zone” harassment of Taiwan has intensified while its military capabilities continue to expand rapidly. The assessment was included in its “Five-Year Force Buildup and Administration Plan Report” (五年兵力整建及施政計畫報告), submitted alongside the defense budget for this year and the “2026 China Military Power Report” (中共軍力報告書). China continues joint combat-readiness patrols, military exercises and China Coast Guard operations, while using maritime militia forces, legal and psychological warfare, and economic coercion. These activities seek to treat the Taiwan Strait as internal waters and strengthen military deterrence against Taiwan, while improving Beijing’s ability to transition from training to combat, the ministry said. An undated photograph shows a Strong Bow anti-ballistic missile (Sky Bow IV) being launched.Photo: Screen grab from the Web site of National Chungshan Institute of Science and Technology The ministry’s domestic priorities include new rifles, night-vision optics, portable counter-drone systems, wheeled combat vehicles and armored fighting vehicles (AFVs). The military is upgrading submarines and testing the domestically built Hai Kun (海鯤), while developing rescue and replenishment vessels, drones and uncrewed boats. It is to procure the Strong Bow (強弓) medium-range anti-tactical ballistic missile system and build a multilayered air-defense network under the “Taiwan Shield” (T-Dome) framework. Other priorities include the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK), upgraded air-combat training systems, digitized command and communications networks, and an islandwide fiber-optic backup network. US procurement priorities include M109A7 self-propelled howitzers and HIMARS multiple-launch rocket systems. The military will continue acquiring Altius 600M and Switchblade 300 systems, and add Altius 600ISR and 700M attack drones. The army has budgeted NT$57.07 billion (US$1.8 billion) from next year to 2033 for 178 domestically developed Cheetah (獵豹) AFVs, armed with 105mm cannons. The D3 prototype has passed evaluation, with procurement to begin next year. The vehicles will have a maximum speed of 100kph, a range of 500km and the ability to fire while moving. The army is also to spend NT$10.7 billion from next year to 2032 on 4,647 light tactical off-road vehicles. Another NT$79.54 billion from next year to 2034 is budgeted to replace aging CM21 armored personnel carriers with 410 wheeled combat and command vehicles. The navy has budgeted NT$18.28 billion from next year to 2032 for a follow-on oil and ammunition replenishment ship. It operates the Panshih (磐石) and Wuyi (武夷), which entered service in 2015 and 1990 respectively, with the Wuyi nearing the end of its service life. It will also spend NT$21.16 billion from next year to 2034 on two follow-on rescue vessels, as existing ships are more than 80 years old. Another NT$13.85 billion is budgeted for a submarine rescue vessel as the Hai Kun and subsequent domestically built submarines enter service. The air force has budgeted NT$36.04 billion this year to 2032 for the Strong Bow medium-range anti-tactical ballistic missile system, previously funded through classified allocations. The system is designed to intercept tactical ballistic missiles at ranges of up to 1,000km and will be integrated with lower-tier systems to form a multilayered defense network. Delivery is scheduled to begin in 2028, although the number of systems remains classified.
